title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description: A **path** in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each adjacent pair is connected by an edge and no node appears more than once. A path does not have to pass through the root. Given the root, return the maximum sum of node values over all non-empty paths.
hints: Any path has a highest node. Consider the best path that 'bends' at each node.
For one node, the best bending path is its value plus the best downward gain from the left and from the right. When is a gain worth taking?
Have a DFS return the best downward path starting at a node (clamping negative gains to 0). At each node update a global best with node + leftGain + rightGain.

solution.explanation: Define gain(node) as the best sum of a downward path starting at node, never worse than 0 because a negative branch can be skipped. A path that bends at node has value node.val + gain(left) + gain(right); track the maximum of this over all nodes. The function returns node.val + max(gain(left), gain(right)) to its parent. One DFS gives O(n) time and O(h) space. Initialise the best to negative infinity so all-negative trees work.
